name: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
title: Programmable Settlement and Escrow
answer: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the rules and code that decide when money moves between parties in a payables or receivables process. It includes conditional payments, milestone releases, holdbacks, deposit escrow, and automated reconciliation when an invoice, delivery note, or approval meets agreed terms. In an AI accounting context, it also covers the models and agents that read contracts, check evidence, and prepare or release a payment instruction. The scope stops at the boundary of the payment rail and the legal escrow arrangement, which remain separate from the software that triggers them.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Programmable settlement and escrow covers the rules and code that decide when money moves between parties in a payables or receivables process. It includes conditional payments, milestone releases, holdbacks, deposit escrow, and automated reconciliation when an invoice, delivery note, or approval meets agreed terms. In an AI accounting context, it also covers the models and agents that read contracts, check evidence, and prepare or release a payment instruction. The scope stops at the boundary of the payment rail and the legal escrow arrangement, which remain separate from the software that triggers them.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a stack that combines an ERP or accounting system, a payment or treasury platform, and a contract or escrow service. Smart contracts on a distributed ledger can hold and release funds, while traditional bank accounts and escrow agents can do the same under a legal agreement. Application programming interfaces connect these systems to invoice capture, identity checks, and document stores. Oracles or integration services feed in external facts such as delivery confirmation, inspection results, or approval status. Key management, access control, and immutable logs sit underneath so that every release can be traced.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work starts by turning contract terms into explicit conditions, such as delivery by a date, acceptance by a named approver, or matching of a purchase order to an invoice. AI models can extract those terms from documents, classify exceptions, and match supporting evidence, but a human or a rule engine usually confirms the condition before funds move. The system then creates a payment instruction, routes it through the chosen rail, and records the settlement against the open payable or receivable. Reconciliation follows, with automated matching of bank or ledger entries and a queue for breaks, disputes, and partial releases. Audit trails capture who or what approved each step and which document version was used.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk in this area turn on authorization, enforceability, and evidence. A clear legal agreement typically states who controls the escrow, what conditions release funds, and how disputes are resolved, because code alone does not create a legal right. Provenance matters for every input, including contract versions, delivery records, model outputs, and approval logs, so that an auditor can reconstruct the decision. Data protection, sanctions screening, anti money laundering checks, and accounting treatment all apply, and the site tracks 215 compliance and regulation pages that touch these duties. Model risk management, segregation of duties, and key custody are part of the control set.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward more continuous settlement, where payment release is tied to real time events rather than monthly cycles. Standards for payment messaging, open banking interfaces, and tokenized deposits are likely to make conditional payments easier to connect across banks and ledgers. AI agents may negotiate terms, verify performance, and prepare settlement instructions, with humans handling exceptions and disputes. Escrow is likely to become a configurable service rather than a standalone account, and audit will move closer to the transaction. The main constraint is not technology but legal recognition, interoperability, and control over who bears the risk when an automated release is wrong.
